dedupe_keys.name: wfp market functionality index mfi market scores from trader surveys by country and market with guidance

description: The Market Functionality Index is WFP's score of how well local markets work, used to decide whether cash-based assistance is viable and to track changes in market functioning over time. The dataset on the Humanitarian Data Exchange gives the index by country and market as a CSV file and bundles the technical guidance, practical guidance with questionnaires in several languages, sampling guidance for the trader survey and a frequently asked questions note. The index is built from trader surveys and scores nine dimensions: assortment of essential goods, availability, price, resilience of supply chains, competition, infrastructure, services, food quality, and access and protection. A nutrition variant, the MFI-N, measures markets' ability to supply nutritious, safe and fortified foods. The data are dated January to June 2026, updated about monthly, and free to download without registration under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Coverage is the countries where WFP runs assessments. Caveats: market samples change between rounds and countries, and scores are relative measures, not volumes or prices. Simulation uses: market functioning scores to set market disruption and recovery states in food supply and humanitarian response models. Related records: WFP global food prices (data-wfp-global-food-prices) and WFP food market locations (data-wfp-food-market-locations) cover prices and market sites.
